5238.moment_proof: For a primal support S of weight w, every weight-8 dual check meets S evenly. Hence sum_D C(|S cap D|,2) >= 300w, while the exact pair codegrees give sum_D C(|S cap D|,2)=25e1+5e2 <=25 C(w,2). Thus w>=25.
5238.weight25_equality: Equality forces every pair of support coordinates into R1 and every dual-check intersection to have size 0 or 2; therefore every weight-25 support is a 25-clique of NO_5^+(5).
5238.equality_consequence: Pass5207's P-heavy exotic weight-625 branch would require a nonzero footprint word of weight <=24 and is therefore impossible. Together with Pass5191, all q5 weight-625 apartment words are the 936 chamber stars.
5238.firewall: This closes the q5 equality shell, not the strict sub-625 distance front.

5241.observed_formula: rank of the PSp4(q) orbital scheme on P-components is (q+3)/2 at q=3,5,7; one special nonadjacent orbital has valency q(q^2-1)/2 and the remaining (q-3)/2 nonadjacent orbitals have valency q(q^2-1).
5241.boundary: The displayed formula is an exact finite-anchor pattern, not yet promoted as an all-odd-q theorem.

5242.statement: Any q5 apartment-code word of weight <625 has zero P-component parity vector.
5242.proof: P parity s lies in C_F. If s is nonzero, Pass5238 gives wt(s)>=25. Each parity-odd P component is nonzero in the local [225,25,25] tensor code and contributes at least 25 apartments, so global weight >=25*25=625.
5242.consequence: The remaining q5 strict distance problem is entirely inside the zero-P-parity sector; Pass5202 may then gauge point parity to zero, although that gauge need not preserve chamber-leader cardinality.

5243.proof: Tensor rank one gives product weights from {5,8,9}; the smallest even product is 5*8=40. Tensor rank at least two has at least d2=9 nonzero rows, each a nonzero Cut(K6) word of weight at least 5, hence weight at least45.
5243.strict_consequence: A q5 word of weight <625 has zero P parity by Pass5242, so every active P component has even local weight >=40; therefore at most 15 P components can be active.

5244.lemma: Let B be an automorphism-invariant family of dual checks for a binary code, with coordinate replication r and maximum distinct-pair codegree lambda. If every primal/check intersection is even, then every nonzero primal word has weight w >= 1+r/lambda.
5244.proof: sum_B C(t_B,2)>=1/2 sum_B t_B=rw/2, while sum_B C(t_B,2)<=lambda C(w,2).
5244.all_q_target: Construct, for odd q, a dual-check orbit with r/lambda=q^2-1. The moment lemma would immediately prove footprint distance q^2.

5245.dual_lower_search: The incidence argument gives d_dual>=9. Fixed-coordinate parity MILPs for weights 9,10,11 are each infeasible; an explicit weight-12 dual word exists.

weight12_geometry.complement: disjoint union of a triangular prism and K3,3

5245.distance_proof: Every primal word meets each weight-12 orbit check evenly. Since the maximum pair codegree is 392, the shell-moment lemma gives w>=1+18816/392=49; point rows have weight49.
5245.boundary: The weight-12 orbit is sufficient for primal d=49; completeness of the entire weight-12 dual shell is not needed and is not claimed.

strict_frontier: q5 equality is now closed: every weight-625 word is a chamber star. q5 strict minimum remains open only in the zero-P-parity sector, where any sub-625 word has at most 15 active P components. Leader36 is not yet eliminated.
literature_boundary: External literature was used only to corroborate the classical PSp4(q) ~= Omega5(q) orthogonal-module viewpoint. No external source located in this run proves the new finite shell-moment distance statements or the q3/q5/q7 orbital data; those are repo computations/proofs.
